answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to prove a long, publicly verifiable chain of sequential modular squarings, where each output is the next input. GPUs can run independent chains, but cannot shorten one chain’s dependency path; an attacker simulating many clones therefore multiplies wall-clock work instead of parallelizing it away. The resulting physical delay makes it costly to forge identities, even when coordination can whisper across a canyon of machines.
